description:
User-directed scope expansion (2026-07-11, review feedback on the signals epic): the CLI has no introspection — `bw signal types` prints bare names; field schemas, enum domains, required_when rules, hook wiring, and timeouts are only discoverable by reading .beadwork/signals.yml; and the only way to test a payload is a real emit, which commits to the beadwork branch.

Advances: bw.signal.config (add introspection requirements/scenarios to the spec as part of this ticket)

Deliverable:
1. `bw signal types [--verbose] [--json]` — default output unchanged (bare names). --verbose: per type render fields (type, enum values, required, required_when), hooks per moment showing per-type AND inherited global with the real resolution order (enrich: global then type; gate: type then global), and the effective hook_timeout. --json: machine-readable equivalent.
2. `bw signal show <type> [--json]` — single-type detail (same info); undefined type is a clear error.
3. `bw signal validate <type> --field k=v... [--run-hooks]` — dry-run. Default: schema validation ONLY (per-field pass/fail report, non-zero exit on invalid); executes NO hooks, stores NOTHING. --run-hooks: additionally executes enrich (report the enriched payload) → final validation → gate (report allow/block/malfunction verdict + captured output); still NEVER stores, and on-blocked does NOT fire in dry-run. Export BW_SIGNAL_DRY_RUN=1 to hook processes in --run-hooks mode so hook authors can guard side effects.
4. Help text for the signal command group updated (additive) in command.go / signal.go usage strings. docs/design.md Signals section gains an Introspection paragraph.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: TestSignalTypesVerbose, TestSignalTypesJSON, TestSignalShowType, TestSignalShowUndefinedType, TestSignalValidateSchemaOnly (valid + invalid payloads), TestSignalValidateNeverStores (explicit suppression-clause test: signals/<ticket>/ empty after validate, with AND without --run-hooks), TestSignalValidateRunHooksGateBlock (gate exit 1 -> reported BLOCKED, nothing stored, on-blocked hook did NOT fire — explicit marker-file assertion), TestSignalValidateDryRunEnv (hook sees BW_SIGNAL_DRY_RUN=1) (cmd/bw and/or internal/signal as fits)
- Spec: ADD introspection must-requirements + scenarios + verification stubs to .spec/specs/signal_config.spec.md and flip stubs as tests land (this ticket may edit that spec beyond stub flips — it introduces the surface).
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: targeted go test ./cmd/bw/... ./internal/signal/... only; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run make preflight, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: flipped stubs + targeted selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test exercising that production path
  - Fixture hygiene: t.TempDir repos, fixed-order fixtures (never map ranging), no cross-test env leakage (BW_SIGNAL_*, BW_SESSION_ID, BW_SIGNAL_DRY_RUN)
  - Every conditional clause covered (verbose/json/plain; defined/undefined type; valid/invalid payload; --run-hooks allow/block; never-store both modes)
  - Negative/suppression clauses get their own explicit tests (never-stores; on-blocked-not-fired)
- Call-site Integration: cmdSignal routing in cmd/bw/signal.go is the production caller for all three subcommand surfaces. Proving tests: TestSignalValidateNeverStores + TestSignalValidateRunHooksGateBlock (drive the real command path).

Out of Scope (files):
- internal/issue/**, internal/intent/**, internal/treefs/**, cmd/bw/signal_query.go, cmd/bw/show.go, internal/md/**, prompts/**
Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- cmd/bw/signal.go
- cmd/bw/signal_test.go
- cmd/bw/command.go (additive help/usage only)
- internal/signal/** (schema accessors / dry-run pipeline mode as needed)
- docs/design.md
- test/acceptance_test.go
- .spec/specs/signal_config.spec.md (may add introspection requirements/scenarios/stubs + flips)

Out of Scope (intent):
- validate must NOT provide any path that stores a signal — dry-run is not a bypass; the emit path's unskippable pipeline is untouched.
- on-blocked and post-emit hooks never execute in dry-run.
- No new external Go dependencies.
- Default `bw signal types` output stays byte-identical (scripts already parse it).
- Emit-path behavior unchanged except factoring shared helpers.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket
